provider: pCloud Premium Plus 2 TB / Ultra 10 TB (lifetime)

free_tier.stated: 500 GB $219; 2 TB $499 (list $709); 10 TB $1,499 (list $2,799). Sale ladders reach 2 TB $299 and 10 TB $890.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: TRAP-SHAPED but escapable. Verbatim from support: 'Every pCloud plan includes a specified amount of shared link traffic that resets on a monthly basis (regardless of whether you have a monthly, annual, or Lifetime subscription) .. pCloud Premium Plus (2 TB): 4 TB per month .. pCloud Ultra (10 TB): 20 TB per month'. Blog confirms the ratio is 2x storage: 'As of September, 2026, it is double the amount of your paid storage'. CRITICAL EXEMPTION: this cap applies only to public shared links. API, WebDAV and app downloads are not counted, per pCloud's own link-traffic explainer.

interface_detail: REST API (api.pcloud.com, probed live: getapiserver returns result 0 with binapi/api hosts), WebDAV, rsync, rclone native `pcloud` backend, FUSE-style virtual drive
tooling: rclone native; WebDAV+rsync documented by vendor
chaining: rclone/WebDAV -> local -> CDN; virtual drive mount is a genuine advantage vs sync-only competitors
limits_note: Constraint type: per-object none; egress is pull-count-ish only on public links. Folder share caps: 150 folder shares/day, 25,000 subfolders or 150,000 files per shared folder.

identity_cost.detail: the account is created with an email address and a verification link, and the vendor's account guidance names an email address and a password; whether registration asks a phone number is unverified. The lifetime plan is bought with a credit or debit card, with PayPal backed by a linked credit or debit card, or with Alipay in select regions

reliability_note: Operates since 2013, Swiss entity. No mass data-loss event. r/DataHoarder 'The Lifetime Trap' thread documents $745 spent and ROI scepticism, not data loss. Payment: card, PayPal, Alipay for select regions; Bitcoin historically accepted (Apple/Google in-app also available).
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.

price_per_tb_month: One-time $249.50/TB at 2 TB ($499); $149.90/TB at 10 TB ($1,499). Amortised over 5 years: $4.16/TB/mo at 2 TB, $2.50/TB/mo at 10 TB. At the $890 sale price for 10 TB: $1.48/TB/mo over 5 years.
